cohort: The study included 217 normal term neonates born between 37 and 42 weeks, excluding those with antenatal risk factors or certain defined conditions, from a Special Care Newborn unit in North India.
finding: Anterior fontanelle size was significantly influenced by gestational maturity only, showing weak positive correlations, and not by weight at birth, head circumference, gender, or mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Neonates born via lower-segment caesarean sections had significantly larger head circumferences compared to those born through normal vaginal delivery, but mode of delivery did not significantly influence AF size.
cross-section timing: during the neonatal period in an outpatient department
